podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakout Band
podcast.body: Jars of Clay was the major breakout act from the alternative Contemporary Christian Music (CCM) movement, achieving significant mainstream success with their hit song "Flood." "They were the big breakout band from what's known as the alternative CCM movement."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Condemnation by Christian Factions
podcast.body: Jars of Clay was among the Christian rock bands that faced condemnation from certain Christian factions who accused them of "perverting Christianity." "And they spend lots of time quoting scripture to support their opinions on the evils and perversions of Creed and jars of clay and MXPX and everybody else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Criticism from within Christian community
podcast.body: Jars of Clay has been subject to condemnation by some individuals who believe that Christian bands, regardless of their message, are perverting Christianity by playing rock music. "And they spend lots of time quoting scripture to support their opinions on the evils and perversions of Creed and jars of clay and MXPX and everybody else."

podcast.title: Paving Way for Others
podcast.body: Jars of Clay's success, particularly with "Flood," helped create opportunities for other bands like DC Talk and Sixpence None the Richer to achieve modest mainstream recognition. "Jarz of Clay paved the way for modest mainstream success by band called DC Talk and then there was six pence none the richer who also had some big singles."
